national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Russian President Vladimir Putin today reviewed the progress in bilateral cooperation in political, economic, defence, energy, space, skill mobility and people-to- people domains. During their bilateral talks in Delhi, the two leaders also shared perspectives on key regional and global issues of mutual interest, including the conflicts in West Asia and the Black Sea region. Prime Minister Modi once again reiterated that dialogue and diplomacy was the way forward in resolving conflicts and India stood ready to assist in peace efforts. External Affairs Ministry said in a statement that Prime Minister Modi and President Putin welcomed Russia’s International Industrial Exhibition “INNOPROM India”. The Exhibition was held for the first time in India from 9th of this month till today, and underscored its importance in further expanding trade and industrial ties. The two leaders also visited the INNOPROM India exhibition and interacted with the participants. The two leaders agreed to remain engaged in an effort to strengthen further the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership between the two countries. The Partnership continues to register significant growth and has shown resilience in the backdrop of geopolitical uncertainties. President Putin invited Prime Minister to visit Russia for the 24th India-Russia Annual Summit. Prime Minister accepted the invitation. The dates of the Summit will be decided as per mutual convenience Mr Modi gifted Mr Putin a Russian translation of the Thirukkural, the ancient Tamil classic by poet-philosopher Thiruvalluvar, during their meeting. It has been published by the Central Institute of Classical Tamil. President Putin arrived in the national capital in the early hours today to attend the BRICS Summit, which begins tomorrow. Prime Minister Modi will hold talks with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian this evening. The meeting assumes significance in view of the prevailing situation in West Asia. Regional developments are expected to be among the key issues to be discussed by the two leaders. Prime Minister Modi is also scheduled to meet UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres during his engagements in National Capital.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | National 91 BRICS nations emerging as important centres of global innovation and solutions, says PM Modi at ...
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that BRICS nations are emerging as important centres of global innovation and solutions. Addressing the Leaders’ Session of BRICS Business Forum at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi this evening, Mr Modi said, today, BRICS nations represent 50 per cent of the world’s population, 40 per cent of its GDP and over 25 per cent of global trade. He said, moreover, while global GDP has grown approximately two-and-a-half-fold over these years, the combined GDP of BRICS nations has expanded nearly four-and-a-half-fold. The Prime Minister said, the economic strength of BRICS has grown at nearly twice the pace of the rest of the world. He said, BRICS nations are also emerging as key hubs for global innovation and solutions. Mr Modi said, new possibilities for innovation, spanning everything from grassroots initiatives to frontier technologies, are taking shape within the countries. The Prime Minister said, amid global uncertainties, India today offers a source of confidence for growth and stability. He called for Make in India, Innovate with India and Scale for the world. He said, at a time when trade barriers are rising across the world, India is building economic bridges. Mr Modi said, global trade can move forward only when sea lanes are secure, supply routes remain open and seafarers are safe. He said, that is why India is a steadfast advocate of freedom of navigation and the safety of seafarers. Mr Modi called upon Member countries to turn BRICS’ ambition into action and the collective strength into solutions for the world.

national_raw_news.title: 5 hours ago | National 130 Stage set for 18th BRICS Summit 2026 beginning tomorrow
national_raw_news.content: The stage is all set for the 18th BRICS Summit to be held at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi tomorrow. During the Summit, Prime Minister Narendra Modi will play host to world leaders including Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping, South African President Cyril Ramaphosa, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto, Iran President Masoud Pezeshkian, and Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed al Nahyan. The theme of India’s Chairship 2026 is Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. The Summit will get underway tomorrow with a Closed Session for BRICS Member Countries on “Inclusive Global Governance and Strengthening Multilateralism”. Leaders of BRICS Member Countries will witness the Bharat Innovates Exhibition at Bharat Mandapam. They will also undertake a joint tree plantation which will be followed by a Gala Dinner hosted by Prime Minister Modi. The Prime Minister will hold a series of bilateral meetings with BRICS leaders on the sidelines of the Summit. On Sunday, Mr Modi will welcome the Leaders of BRICS Partner Countries and Outreach Invitees. The Leaders will participate in a Session on “Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability: Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth”. Our correspondent reports that India’s 2026 BRICS Chairship comes at a time of significant global transformation. The international system is experiencing economic fragmentation, technological disruption and geopolitical uncertainty. Climate change and resource pressures are adding further complexity. These interconnected challenges require cooperation that is inclusive, practical and responsive to diverse national circumstances. India’s Chairship seeks to build consensus across diverse members while strengthening the effectiveness of existing mechanisms. India aims to reinforce BRICS as a constructive force for a more inclusive global order.

national_raw_news.title: India’s demographic dividend visible in rapidly growing fintech ecosystem, says FM Sitharaman 2 hours ago 63
national_raw_news.content: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has said that India should pursue technological innovation at scale, but without compromising human responsibility, safety and public trust. Addressing the Global Fintech Festival 2026, the Finance Minister said India’s young generation was not waiting for opportunities but was creating platforms, enterprises and new solutions. She said India’s demographic dividend was visible in the country’s rapidly growing technology and fintech ecosystem. Smt. Sitharaman also questioned those who view India’s demographic dividend through a lens of perpetual pessimism. Referring to sceptics in a lighter vein, she said “naraz fufa jis” are never short of reasons to doubt India’s moment and capabilities. Highlighting the challenges posed by emerging technologies, the Finance Minister described Artificial Intelligence as a double-edged sword. She said AI can help detect fraud faster, but can also enable perpetrators to automate larger and more sophisticated frauds. Finance Minister stressed the need for greater institutional accountability in the development and deployment of Artificial Intelligence. She said speed and efficiency should not come at the cost of safety, transparency and human oversight. Regulators, boards and senior management, she said, must understand how AI is used, the decisions it influences and the risks involved. She also called for stronger cybersecurity, data protection, consumer protection and cooperation between regulators and innovators. The Finance Minister said the success of India’s fintech sector should be measured not only by transactions and valuations, but also by the trust it earns and the problems it solves. Smt. Sitharaman also urged the Reserve Bank of India to further advance its wholesale and retail Central Bank Digital Currency pilots, citing the growing momentum in tokenisation and digital finance.

national_raw_news.title: Rise in BRICS countries’ exports to $6 trillion in 2024 reflects its potential : Piyush Goyal 3 hours ago 87
national_raw_news.content: The Leaders’ Session of BRICS Business Forum is underway at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. Heads of State of BRICS Member Countries including Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Russian President Vladimir Putin, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and South African President Cyril Ramaphosa are attending the session. In his address, Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal said that during India’s Chairship, BRICS has been driven by a clear purpose, to achieve more balanced trade amongst member nations and to explore expansion of trade in services across the bloc. He said exports from BRICS countries have risen from about USD 900 billion in 2003 to USD 6 trillion in 2024, reflecting the scale of its market and potential. He said, under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India remains committed to ensure that this cooperation reaches those who form the backbone of the BRICS economies . Mr Goyal said, it must benefit the farmers, empower women in business and beyond and provide greater opportunities for wealth and prosperity to young entrepreneurs and MSMEs. He said, with the participation over two thousand business leaders and delegates from member countries and partner countries, this is the largest BRICS Business Forum ever held. He mentioned that the Forum has taken up issues such as non-tariff barriers, impacting global value chains, agriculture and agri-technology, services trade, women-led enterprises and the digital economy.
